pageCache.pageTitle: Mayesbrook Park School - Our vision and ethos
pageCache.text:
About us
Our vision and ethos
At Mayesbrook Park School, our mission is to provide a transformational education for our students that will engage, nurture, challenge and empower them to make positive choices.
We believe that all our students can be happy and successful, and we develop their confidence and independence to move forward purposefully to school, college and employment.
Developing positive relationships and trust across the school community is at the heart of our ethos.
Our first-class curriculum, and the high expectations we have of our students, gives them the opportunity to progress academically and to develop the personal qualities of self-awareness, self-regulation, honesty, resilience, and respect for others.
We value and develop the capacity of our students to take on responsibility and leadership, and we listen to their voices.

Outreach Tuition Plus

Rectroy Campus
Welcome to the Rectory Campus
The Rectory Campus is the home of the Outreach Tuition Plus service.
Outreach Tuition Plus offers access to education to children temporarily unable to attend full time school because of illness, exceptional circumstances or the unavailability of a suitable school place.
Tuition is a short-term intervention - it is not an alternative to full-time school. Learning is personalised and delivered on a 1.1 basis. The goal of tuition is to prepare the student for a successful transition into a full-time education. Students referred to us range from reception age through to 16.
Tuition may take place online, at the Rectory Campus or in the student’s home. Students may have a hybrid offer involving part time attendance at their school.
The Rectory campus has been specifically designed for tuition and is a purposefully quiet and peaceful environment. Students have access to 1.1 learning spaces, a sensory space, an art space, food technology space and space for physical movement.
If Tuition is online our school home support officer will make regular welfare visits to see the child in person.
Tuition is reviewed at regular intervals to assess the readiness of the student to return to full time education. Where medical conditions persist, professional opinion is sought and parents will be required to provide appropriate certification or evidence of ongoing conditions.

About us
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to Mayesbrook Park School, an alternative provision school based in Barking and Dagenham, east London, with three campuses – Mayesbrook Park, Erkenwald and Seabrook.
We provide full-time education and support from Years 7 to 11 (reception to Year 11 via our Access to Education Service - formerly the Home Tuition Service) for 11- to 16-year-olds who have had difficulties with their learning and behaviour in mainstream school. Some students are with us for a few months, others throughout their secondary schooling.
At Mayesbrook Park School, we aim to give all our students the necessary skills to move forward successfully into the next phase of their lives – be that reintegration into mainstream school, further education or employment.
Through our balanced curriculum, personalised support and enrichment activities, we encourage students to engage with their studies. Through our team of skilled teachers and learning support staff, we help reduce their barriers to learning. And through our high expectations, we challenge our students to succeed.
As well as growing academically, we want our students to develop emotionally and socially so they can contribute to the wider community. We listen to them, encourage them to take on responsibilities, and we work to develop positive relationships and mutual trust across our school. We also work closely with parents/carers and outside agencies to create a safe, secure and enjoyable learning environment where students are encouraged to reach their full potential.
I am pleased to say that our most recent Ofsted report in November 2018 grades us as good in all areas and recognises our 'culture of high expectations and success' where 'staff at all levels are very supportive of the ethos of the school and the vision for the future'. Moving forward, we will be striving to further improve by bringing greater depth to our teaching and curriculum and giving excellent attendance a higher profile.
I hope you enjoy reading about our work. If you need more information (or free paper copies of anything that appears on this website), please get in touch via our contact section.
Cathy StygalHeadteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Mayesbrook Park School - Welcome from the Head of Campus
pageCache.text:
Erkenwald Campus
Welcome from the Head of Campus
Welcome to Erkenwald Campus, which along with Mayesbrook Park and Seabrook Campuses, is part of Mayesbrook Park School in Barking and Dagenham.
At Erkenwald, we provide education and support for up to 40 students aged 11 to 16 who are struggling to attend mainstream school due to underlying emotional and mental health issues, and require a smaller, more nurturing setting. Where possible, we aim to help them return to mainstream provision or ensure that their post-16 choices are successful and secure. We also provide a Outreach Tuition Plus service for students who are too ill to attend school due to physical or mental health issues.
Our mission is to ensure that our students are given the same opportunities as their peers to reach their academic and personal potential. Most of our students have very low attendance when they join us. Many have low self-esteem and self-confidence; others have experienced social exclusion, bullying and disrupted lives at school and/or at home. All require intensive support from both Erkenwald staff and external agencies to grow both academically and personally.
We offer a range of courses for our students with a focus on the core subjects. We expect them to make at least good and, where possible, accelerated progress during their time with us. Our experienced staff challenge them through personalised academic programmes and a variety of inspiring extra-curricular activities to develop their self-esteem and confidence. Students respond well to the calm, inclusive ethos at the campus and build positive, trusting relationship with their peers and staff
Our strength lies in our holistic approach to students’ well-being; services such as Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services, our Special Educational Needs and Disability team, educational psychology services, our safeguarding team and on-site Family Support Professional can all be called upon to work together to support our young people and their families.
Erkenwald Campus is a very special place. The staff and I work tirelessly to provide a safe and healing environment, and to empower our students to re-engage with their education and grow their self-confidence to meet life’s challenges and opportunities – now and in the future.
Elizabeth BaileyHead of Campus

Mayesbrook Park Campus
Welcome from the Head Teacher
Welcome to Mayesbrook Park Campus. We provide up to 70 full-time places for 11 to 16 year-olds who have been excluded permanently or short term, or are on respite placements from their mainstream school.
Many of the students referred to our campus have experienced behavioural, emotional or social difficulties in their previous schools. We work to support them to return to mainstream schooling or, for more vocational learners, to take up a college place.
We offer a supportive, caring environment to help them to overcome their barriers to learning. Our highly experienced staff are key to that success and want students to do well. Mentoring and counselling opportunities are available if required, and our students value all the adults’ support and care. Students generally follow a curriculum similar to that of mainstream schools and have the chance to study GCSEs in seven or more subjects, with additional non-accredited subjects available to broaden the curriculum.
We have high expectations of behaviour and engagement in our school, and regularly reward and celebrate those who put in consistent effort and try their best. In the last year, we sent students on three residential trips, and regular team-building activities help them to build trust and confidence. Our students also take part in borough sports events, supporting young people with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. We encourage them to make positive contributions to their local community.
We also work very closely with parents/carers and partner organisations to support our students and their family to move from what is often a negative place to a more positive point in their lives.
Our overall aim is to encourage and support students to develop a sense of self-worth and aspirations for the future, to recognise that mistakes can be overcome and that they can still achieve at the highest levels. We want all of our students to know that being at Mayesbrook Park Campus is a stepping stone to a brighter future, as they will have learnt from the hurdles they have overcome and become stronger characters, determined to fulfil their potential.
Our real mark of success is when ex-students return and tell us how well they are doing in their new school, college or workplace, and that their time here was a real turning point for them.
If you would like to see the good things we get involved in and to meet our students, please contact the campus office to arrange a visit.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mayesbrook Park School - Welcome to the Campus
pageCache.text:
Seabrook Campus
Welcome to the Campus
Welcome to the Seabrook Campus. Here we provide a bespoke education offer for a small group of mainly Key Stage 4 students. The students have often been struggling with social, emotional or mental health issues which have impacted on their progress in other areas of our school or their previous school and may therefore mean that they are in danger of permanent exclusion.
Our bespoke curriculum focuses on supporting students to build their confidence and enable them to complete their GCSEs in a smaller environment, more suited to their needs.
Each school day begins with Breakfast Club and small group discussion in order to best prepare for the day ahead.
The curriculum offer allows for core subjects - English, maths and science, along with History, PSHE and other subjects as suited to individual student needs. In addition each student has access to the school counsellor, mentoring and other targeted support services. This ensures that we provide a holistic approach to learning to prepare our students for life beyond Mayesbrook Park School.
Students will all have access to careers advice and work with a transition coach to support them through year 11 and ongoing in years 12 and 13, to help them to sustain their next placement.
Our committed, highly qualified staff are trained to teach in alternative provision, to mentor and to meet students’ individual needs.
Positive relationships, mutual trust and respect are key to a successful programme at Seabrook. We value our students and listen to their ideas and opinions. In return, we have high expectations of their behaviour and commitment to their progress. We work closely with parents/carers and our partner organisations to help our students and their families deal with any issues they might have.
We believe that all our students can be happy and successful, and we support them to build their confidence and self-esteem so they are ready to re-engage successfully with their education and achieve their full potential.
For more information on our campus, please contact us by clicking here.
Cathy Stygal Dawid Hetnal Linda Brown Headteacher Lead teacher Assistant Headteacher/SENDCo

pageCache.pageTitle: Mayesbrook Park School - Mayesbrook Park School Careers Programme
pageCache.text:
About us
Careers Programme
At Mayesbrook Park School we want our students to gain the knowledge of what is possible
Mayesbrook Park School believes that good CEIAG (careers education, information, advice and guidance) connects learning to the future. It motivates young people by giving them a clearer idea of the routes to jobs and careers that they will find engaging and rewarding. Good CEIAG widens pupils’ horizons, challenges stereotypes and raises aspirations. It provides pupils with the knowledge and skills necessary to make successful transitions to the next stage of their life. This supports social mobility by improving opportunities for all young people.
We want to ensure that we source the right providers to deliver meaningful and thought provoking workshops that inspire our students to achieve their full potential. To build collaborative relationships and networking opportunities that better serve our young people including visits to FE/HE. To have better employer links with real work experience opportunities. We strive to give our students the necessary tools so that they are better prepared for post 16 options when they leave us.
Here at Mayesbrook Park School we are working hard to meet the expectations set out in the Gatsby Benchmarks;
In the last academic year (2023/24) our school was part of the Mayor's Young Londoners Fund 'Back on Track' programme, organised by 15billionebp. This provides a wide range of support to students, funding workshops on employability, confidence building and issues affecting young people. This partnership has enabled our students to have the opportunity to visit employers, Uni visits, attend workshops and mock interviews. We were proud to take part in a work experience pilot for Alternative Provision with 15billionebp which was really successful and we hope to be able to offer similar programmes to our students in the future.
Mayesbrook Park School works with an experienced independent careers advisor who meets with all KS4 students across our School to offer careers information and guidance. KS3 students have access to our careers advisor when she is on site. We host a careers fair annually where students can meet with local colleges and providers and discuss opportunities with them in more detail. Students will have support in completing application forms and signing up for apprenticeships and college open events. Post 16 options and preparation is discussed across the curriculum.
Mayesbrook Park has a Transition Team with Transition Coaches who closely support our year 11's whilst preparing them for their post 16 destination. The team will then continue to work with the students after they have left us in Years 12 and 13 to ensure a smooth transition into employment, education and training. This continued support will include regular contact and visits to students. We hope to support students in sustaining their placements. Data from our students' destinations will be used to improve the effectiveness of our careers programme.
Over the coming year our focus will be Gatsby Benchmarks one, five and seven. We are working closely with the Careers & Enterprise Company to implement a stable careers programme. We are also part of the Local Future Careers Cluster. Organised by 15billionebp and funded by the Mayor of London/GLA and the European Social Fund, this network of 12 schools and colleges in Newham and Barking and Dagenham are provided with careers support in the form of needs analyses, careers education pilot programmes, funded work experience placements and careers strategies.
Staff, Student and parent feedback is regularly obtained so that we continuously improve our offer. We review our careers programme annually and this will be reviewed in July 2025. We also evaluate our programme termly against the Gatsby Benchmarks to assess our progress in these areas.
Please feel free to contact our Careers Leader on the details below if you have any questions about our careers offer.
Rachel Atkins - 14-16 Colleges and Vocational Programmes Manager

pageCache.pageTitle: Mayesbrook Park School - Personal Development Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Personal Development
Intent
PSHEE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education) and RSE (Relationships and Sex Education) at Mayesbrook Park School aim to extend beyond the academic, technical and vocational. We support and encourage students to develop in many diverse aspects of life. We recognise that students are influenced by factors other than school and aim to teach students how to develop their confidence and resilience in an ever developing world.
We recognise the part we play in preparing pupils for adult life, teaching them how to engage with society and providing them with the opportunities to do so.
To do this we provide access to vital information about the students themselves and the many facets of the diverse world around them. We provide a tailored curriculum that is both broad and balanced, whilst meeting the unique context of our school. This subject is delivered to all students across all campuses at both KS3 and KS4.
Students are introduced to the core topics of PSHEE as prescribed by the PSHE association and statutory guidance of Living in the Wider World, Relationships and Health & Wellbeing. From the Spring term of year 10, students are introduced to the Health and Social Care SOW to prepare them for their Tech Award exam in year 11.
New arrivals
All students are fully supported to ensure that they can make adequate steps to catch- up on the curriculum. Teachers and LSPs take the time to meet with students to bring them up-to-date with the content being delivered.
Implementation
Differentiated PSHEE/Health & Social Care lessons are taught weekly to all students across the 3 sites with Mrs Waite leading as the subject specialist. Students have access to high-quality teaching as well as various external agencies visiting to provide specialist workshops and lessons. This includes SubWize, Come Correct, Fearless and Street Doctors to name a few.
The use of novels is key to the PSHEE curriculum. Throughout the autumn term, students study a novel and explore its key themes and content. This is then used throughout the year to provide contextual background to abstract issues which are covered. This provides a sense of safety and security for students by externalising challenging topics.
In recognition of the changing needs of our students, we have moved from a 100% coursework qualification to a Tech Award in Health & Social Care. This will allow us to meet all statutory requirements outlined by the DfE, as well as broadening the curriculum whilst ensuring that all students, regardless of their entry point, have the best opportunity for success.
We promote equality of opportunity so that all pupils can thrive together, understanding that difference is a positive, not a negative. We ensure that an inclusive environment is offered at all times and place a significant focus on teaching about equality and protected characteristics, in the classroom and beyond. We develop and deepen students' understanding of the fundamental British values through the curriculum, assemblies and wider opportunities.
Careers provision is provided in liaison with the schools careers/transition team. Together we encourage students to make good choices and understand what they need to do to succeed in the careers to which they aspire. Opportunities are provided for students in all year groups to access a range of education and training providers to inform them about technical education qualifications and apprenticeships. Unbiased careers advice and guidance is provided by the team, in liaison with external specialist services.
Impact
It is important to consider that the impact of the personal development curriculum may not be assessable during a student's time at school. We recognise, however, that it is important to acknowledge the hard work students do during their time with us. Therefore, all students have the opportunity to achieve a Level 1/2 Tech Award in Health and Social Care, as well as various Unit Awards through the AQA Unit Award Scheme.
PSHEE/Health & Social Care are subjects which impact on students personally, socially, morally and culturally as well as academically. Students leave Mayesbrook Park School able to reflect on their own beliefs and experiences, with a developed sense of morality and a deeper sense of understanding consequences of their behaviour and actions. This, in turn, supports them to use a range of social skills in different contexts with the ability to recognise and value the things we share in common across the socio-economic community they are members of.
Assessment within PSHEE/Health & Social Care lessons will ensure that students are building on their skills & knowledge over time. It will demonstrate progression and also uniformity across campuses. Predetermined assessment objectives allow teachers to be mindful of assessment elements within lessons and can help to pitch and plan subsequent lessons in liaison with stakeholders. KS4 students complete 2 coursework assignments, as well as 1 formal examination to gain the Tech Award at Level 1/2.
Activities are included within lessons to provide students the opportunity to self and peer-assess which gives them the opportunity to identify areas for self-development. pageCache.pageTitle: Mayesbrook Park School - Personal Development Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Personal Development
Intent
PSHEE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education) and RSE (Relationships and Sex Education) at Mayesbrook Park School aim to extend beyond the academic, technical and vocational. We support and encourage students to develop in many diverse aspects of life. We recognise that students are influenced by factors other than school and aim to teach students how to develop their confidence and resilience in an ever developing world. We recognise the part we play in preparing pupils for adult life, teaching them how to engage with society and providing them with the opportunities to do so.
To do this we provide access to vital information about the students themselves and the many facets of the diverse world around them. We provide a tailored curriculum that is both broad and balanced, whilst meeting the unique context of our school. This subject is delivered to all students across all campuses at both KS3 and KS4. Students are introduced to the core topics of PSHEE as prescribed by the PSHE association and statutory guidance of Living in the Wider World, Relationships and Health & Wellbeing. From the Spring term of year 10, students are introduced to the Health and Social Care SOW to prepare them for their Tech Award exam in year 11.
New arrivals
All students are fully supported to ensure that they can make adequate steps to catch- up on the curriculum. Teachers and LSPs take the time to meet with students to bring them up-to-date with the content being delivered.
Implementation
Differentiated PSHEE/Health & Social Care lessons are taught weekly to all students across the 3 sites with Mrs Waite leading as the subject specialist. Students have access to high-quality teaching as well as various external agencies visiting to provide specialist workshops and lessons. This includes SubWize, Come Correct, Fearless and Street Doctors to name a few.
The use of novels is key to the PSHEE curriculum. Throughout the autumn term, students study a novel and explore its key themes and content. This is then used throughout the year to provide contextual background to abstract issues which are covered. This provides a sense of safety and security for students by externalising challenging topics.
In recognition of the changing needs of our students, we have moved from a 100% coursework qualification to a Tech Award in Health & Social Care. This will allow us to meet all statutory requirements outlined by the DfE, as well as broadening the curriculum whilst ensuring that all students, regardless of their entry point, have the best opportunity for success. We promote equality of opportunity so that all pupils can thrive together, understanding that difference is a positive, not a negative. We ensure that an inclusive environment is offered at all times and place a significant focus on teaching about equality and protected characteristics, in the classroom and beyond. We develop and deepen students' understanding of the fundamental British values through the curriculum, assemblies and wider opportunities.
Careers provision is provided in liaison with the schools careers/transition team. Together we encourage students to make good choices and understand what they need to do to succeed in the careers to which they aspire. Opportunities are provided for students in all year groups to access a range of education and training providers to inform them about technical education qualifications and apprenticeships. Unbiased careers advice and guidance is provided by the team, in liaison with external specialist services.
Impact
It is important to consider that the impact of the personal development curriculum may not be assessable during a student's time at school. We recognise, however, that it is important to acknowledge the hard work students do during their time with us. Therefore, all students have the opportunity to achieve a Level 1/2 Tech Award in Health and Social Care, as well as various Unit Awards through the AQA Unit Award Scheme.
PSHEE/Health & Social Care are subjects which impact on students personally, socially, morally and culturally as well as academically. Students leave Mayesbrook Park School able to reflect on their own beliefs and experiences, with a developed sense of morality and a deeper sense of understanding consequences of their behaviour and actions. This, in turn, supports them to use a range of social skills in different contexts with the ability to recognise and value the things we share in common across the socio-economic community they are members of.
Assessment within PSHEE/Health & Social Care lessons will ensure that students are building on their skills & knowledge over time. It will demonstrate progression and also uniformity across campuses. Predetermined assessment objectives allow teachers to be mindful of assessment elements within lessons and can help to pitch and plan subsequent lessons in liaison with stakeholders. KS4 students complete 2 coursework assignments, as well as 1 formal examination to gain the Tech Award at Level 1/2.
Activities are included within lessons to provide students the opportunity to self and peer-assess which gives them the opportunity to identify areas for self-development. Teacher and pupil dialogue is viewed to be of paramount importance. Ipsative, summative and formative assessment formats are all used.

Curriculum
Music Curriculum
Intent
The music curriculum at MPS is designed for students to be exposed to a creative curriculum whilst they also learn useful life skills such as: focus, creativity, communication skills, dedication, perseverance, confidence, collaboration, resilience and determination. This empowers students to build on musical knowledge and skills including performing, composing, recording and appraising.
We pride ourselves in providing unique learning experiences for our young people to expand their horizon and give them the opportunity to learn, grow, and share ideas with others during musical activities, African drumming workshops, events, trips AQA Unit Award and the Level 2 NCFE qualification.
We aim to make our music curriculum as cross curricular as possible by encouraging students to use the knowledge and skills they are acquiring in other subjects to help support their learning of music. For example the use of literacy skills to write reviews/lyrics and mathematics in counting bars, beats alongside composition and timings. Parents evenings, phone calls and In Touch ensure that parents are kept informed.
Implemention
Our bespoke music curriculum is guided by the NCFE qualification framework and encourages in the students’ knowledge of current and relevant music to engage and stimulate students ‘love for learning’. By developing a meaningful teacher- student relationship we are able to engage students through music production and other resources.
We use a combination of composing, performing, and listening which are all key aspects of musical knowledge, skills, and understanding to build an awareness of music technology. Through a variety of topics the students are then able to build on their knowledge and are able to recognise different genres and styles of music. We aim to develop independent learning, understanding personal, social, intellectual and cultural development.
Catch-up - As part of blended learning, a sequence of lessons will be available to support students in class as well as those working remotely. Online resources are structured to maintain students' well-being and to keep them stimulated. Students will be able to access learning remotely via the Google classroom app and hard copies. Learning will be project based to encourage participation and engagement whilst still allowing them to develop musical skills, independent thinking skills and IT skills. These options will provide opportunities to collect evidence for half-termly assessments and Level 2 NCFE assessments.
Implementation of blended learning - To focus on technical knowledge and skills through performances and collaborative work that students are unable to access through remote learning, to further develop and engage students through the use of extra-curricular opportunities, formative and summative assessments to establish where the gaps in learning are and continue to use the remote learning platform to deliver targeted homework/self-regulated study.
Impact
Our aim is that all students participating in music will be engaged and inspired to develop a ‘love of music’ and their talent as musicians, and to increase their self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement.
We believe music has the potential to have a profound impact on students’ development by promoting cultural capital, increasing confidence and self-esteem, developing leadership, team working, concentration and problem-solving skill all of which help with successful transitions post-16 and develop identity and improving social cohesion within the school and wider community.
Students will build skills on taking an active role and interaction in their learning to become better independent learners. These attributes all enhance their opportunities for further education and employability. Additionally we hope to provide access to learning by improving student’s subject knowledge, hand-eye coordination, develop motor skills, make the learning relatable, challenge and support the needs of each individual.
